description: Electricity, magnetism, optics, and modern physics.
notes: Presented in a two-semester algebra/trigonometry based sequence. Physics 180B not open to students with credit in

title: Physical Measurements Laboratory
description: A laboratory course to accompany PHYS 180B Electricity, DC circuits, oscilloscope measurement techniques, electric and magnetic fields, and optics.

title: Principles of Physics
description: Fundamental principles of physics in areas of mechanics and oscillatory motion. Designed for students requiring calculus-based physics.
notes: Recommended: High school physics or PHYS 180A.

title: Principles of Physics Laboratory
description: Experiments in mechanics, wave motion, resonance phenomena using precision air tracks. Not open to students with credit in

title: Principles of Physics
description: Fundamental principles of physics in areas of electricity and magnetism. Designed for students requiring calculus-based physics.

title: Principles of Physics Laboratory
description: Experiments in DC circuits, AC circuits, electrical resonance, oscilloscope measurement techniques, and electric and magnetic fields.

title: Principles of Physics
description: Fundamental principles of physics in areas of electromagnetic waves, modern physics, optics, relativity, thermodynamics, and wave motion. Designed for students requiring calculus-based physics.

title: Principles of Physics Laboratory
description: Experiments in optics, lasers, holography, and nuclear counting.

title: Experimental Topics
description: Selected topics.

title: Special Study
description: Individual study.

title: Electronics for Scientists
description: Series/parallel circuits, Kirchhoff’s law, Maxwell’s loop, voltage dividers, Thevenin and Norton circuits, RC, RL and RLC circuits, Analog and digital scopes, Coaxial lines, Semiconductor devices: diodes and transistors, operational amplifiers and limitations, ADC, Digital sampling theory, Limitations of measurement instrumentation.

title: Introduction to Computational Physics
description: Numerical methods applied to a variety of physics topics. Use of computers to solve and plot problems involving differential equations, matrices, root finding, numerical integration.

title: Classical Mechanics
description: Newtonian mechanics, gravitation, small oscillations, collisions, motion of rigid bodies, Lagrangian mechanics.

title: Modern Physics
description: Special theory of relativity. Particle properties of electromagnetic radiation, and wave properties of particles. Introduction to quantum theory with applications to atomic structure.

title: Advanced Physical Measurements
description: Stresses both laboratory experiments and techniques of data and error analysis. Experiments are taken from major areas of physics.

title: Thermal Physics
description: Classical thermodynamics and statistical mechanics. Applications of equilibrium thermodynamics. Statistical mechanics, including concepts from probability and statistics. Maxwell-Boltzmann, Fermi-Dirac, and Bose-Einstein statistics. Applications of statistical mechanics in calculating macroscopic properties of simple systems.

title: Classical Electromagnetism
description: Electrostatics, magnetostatics, electromagnetic induction, Maxwell’s equations, radiation and wave propagation.

title: Classical Electromagnetism
description: Electrostatics, magnetostatics, electromagnetic induction, Maxwell’s equations, radiation and wave propagation.

title: Optics
description: Reflection, refraction, matrix methods, dispersion, polarization, double refraction, interference, diffraction, Fourier optics, coherence theory, lasers, and holography with applications to optical instruments, wave propagation, and the nature of light.

title: Quantum Mechanics
description: Mathematical and physical foundations of quantum theory in terms of wave and matrix mechanics. Applications to properties of atoms and solids.

title: Processes and Inquiry in Physics
description: Investigation of processes of inquiry and rational thinking skills characteristic of physics, focusing on energy transformations, heat transfer and thermodynamics, force and motion, electricity and magnetism, and waves.

title: Selected Topics in Physics
description: Selected topics in classical and modern physics.

title: Senior Research
description: Selection and design of individual research project. Oral and written progress reports.

title: Senior Research
description: Laboratory work, progress reports, oral and written final reports.

title: Special Study
description: Individual study or laboratory work on a special problem in physics selected by the student. Each student will be assigned a member of the staff who will supervise his/her work.
notes: Credit, hours and topics to be arranged in each case.

title: Condensed Matter Physics
description: Elastic, electric, magnetic, optical, and thermal properties of solids. Energy band theory of solids and practical application with metals and semiconductors.

title: Modern Optics and Lasers
description: Electromagnetic theory, matrix methods of optics, propagation of Gaussian beams, optical resonators, interaction of radiation and atomic systems, theory of laser oscillation, nonlinear optics, specific laser systems, optical detectors, applications of lasers in physics.

title: Modern Optics Laboratory
description: Experiments in various fields of modern optics such as holography, physics of lasers, Fourier transform spectroscopy, Raman spectroscopy, light modulation techniques, fiber optics, spatial filtering, diffraction grating spectroscopy, radiometry, and nonlinear optics.

title: Radiological Physics and Dosimetry
description: Ionizing radiation fields, interactions of radiation with matter, cavity theory, external radiation dosimetry.

title: Nuclear Physics
description: Nuclear and elementary particle phenomena including nuclear structure, decay, and radioactivity. Nuclear reactions and devices. Experimental methods and applications.

title: Radiobiology and Radiation Safety
description: Effects of ionizing radiation on physical and biological systems in medical imaging and radiation therapy. Associated radiation safety precautions.

title: Nuclear Medicine Physics
description: Physical principles of nuclear medicine and operating principles of nuclear medicine instrumentation. Radionuclide production, dose calibrators, well counters, gamma cameras, SPECT, PET, image quality, tomographic reconstruction, and image processing.

title: Relativity
description: Relative coordinates, Lorentz transformation, covariant formation of the laws of physics, applications of special relativity, introduction to curved space time, cosmology.

title: Computational Physics
description: Computer programming for numerical solution of problems in classical mechanics, electromagnetism, optics, and quantum mechanics. Use of Fortran and C programming languages and the UNIX operating system. Incorporation of standard subroutines for linear algebra and differential equations into student written programs.

title: Introduction to Quantum Computing
description: Overview of quantum computing and quantum information. Quantum mechanics of spin systems and qubits; entanglement, superposition, and measurement. Basic quantum circuits and their applications and physical implementation. Quantum cryptography. History, potential applications, and near-future prospects.
notes: Not open to students with credit or concurrent enrollment in PHYS 681, COMP 581, or COMP 681.

title: Special Topics in Physics
description: Selected topics in classical and modern physics.

title: Electromagnetic Theory
description: Electrostatics, magnetic induction, and magnetostatics, Maxwell’s equations, electromagnetic waves and radiation, fields in macroscopic media, special relativity.

title: Statistical Mechanics
description: Statistical basis of thermodynamics. Microcanonical, canonical, and grand canonical ensembles. Ideal Bose and Fermi systems. Interacting systems. Phase transitions.

title: Classical Mechanics
description: Vector and tensor methods, motion of rigid bodies, vibration, coupled circuits, Lagrange’s and Hamilton’s equations, principle of least action.

title: Quantum Mechanics
description: Physical and mathematical basis of quantum mechanics. Wave mechanics and the Schroedinger Equation, matricies and Hilbert space, angular momentum and spin, atomic structure, bound-state perturbation theory, many particle systems, transition rates and time-dependent perturbation theory, scattering, and relativistic quantum mechanics.

title: Medical Physics
description: Radiological physics, dosimetry, imaging, and radiation protection in medical environments including diagnostic radiology, nuclear medicine, and radiation oncology.

title: Medical Physics
description: Radiological physics, dosimetry, imaging, and radiation protection in medical environments including diagnostic radiology, nuclear medicine, and radiation oncology.

title: Radiation Therapy Physics Laboratory
description: Skills to perform radiation therapy physics procedures.

title: Diagnostic Imaging Laboratory
description: Skills to perform quality assurance and acceptance testing on radiological equipment in a clinical setting.

title: Radiation Treatment Planning
description: Fundamental and practical concepts in radiation treatment planning. Hands on experience in clinical treatment planning for external beam radiotherapy.

title: Quantum Computing
description: Overview of quantum computing and quantum information. Quantum mechanics of spin systems and qubits; entanglement, superposition, and measurement. Basic and intermediate quantum circuits and their applications and physical implementation. Quantum cryptography. Simulation of quantum circuits. History, potential applications, and near-future prospects.
notes: Requires use of Python programming. Not open to students with credit or concurrent enrollment in PHYS 581, COMP 581, or COMP 681.

title: Advanced Topics in Physics
description: Intensive study in specific areas of physics.

title: Clinical Rotations I
description: On-site, full-day clinical training in external beam modalities (megavoltage photons, electrons, superficial x-rays) including equipment selection, radiation protection, acceptance/commissioning, calibration and quality assurance. Theoretical basis and use of the various detectors and dosimeters associated with external beam modalities.

title: Clinical Rotations II
description: On-site, full-day clinical training in intensity modulated radiation therapy (IMRT) and brachytherapy. Training in quality assurance, calibration, inverse planning, IMRT delivery, and radiation safety. Radionuclides and sealed sources in brachytherapy, clinical applications of the sources, treatment planning, and quality assurance.

title: Clinical Rotations III
description: On-site, full-day clinical training in the principles of computed tomography (CT) simulator, associated radiation protection/design considerations, CT protocols. Understand the physics of imaging modalities and perform quality assurance on CT, MRI, ultrasound and PET as related to radiation therapy. Train on picture archiving and communication systems.

title: Clinical Rotations IV
description: On-site, full-day clinical training covering physics concepts and implementation of standard radiation treatment (RT) techniques for common cancer treatment sites, routine quality assurance associated with patient specific RT and planning, special RT procedures, quality assurance of RT planning systems, patient safety with respect to radiation therapy.

title: Research
description: Research in one of the fields of physics.

title: Special Study
description: Individual study.

title: Thesis
description: Preparation of a thesis in physics for the master’s degree.

title: Thesis Extension
description: Registration required in any semester or term following assignment of RP in Course 799A in which the student expects to use the facilities and resources of the university; also student must be registered in the course when the completed thesis is granted final approval.

title: Comprehensive Examination Extension
description: Registration required of students whose only requirement is completion of the comprehensive examination for the master’s degree. Registration in 799C limited to two semesters.
